overview: Rinchenia (named in honour of Mongolian palaeontologist Rinchen Barsbold) was a small oviraptorosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia, living approximately 72–66 million years ago (Maastrichtian). Named by Barsbold in 1997, it is estimated at about 2.5 metres in length and is known from a skull and fragmentary postcranial material from the Nemegt Formation of Omnogov province. It is distinguished by a very tall, elaborate cranial crest.

Rinchenia belongs to Oviraptoridae within the Oviraptorosauria and is placed within the subfamily Oviraptorinae and tribe Citipatinae. Its highly developed crest is one of the most elaborate among oviraptorids and may have functioned in display or species recognition. The genus was originally described as a species of Oviraptor (O. mongoliensis) but was reclassified as a distinct genus following recognition of its unique crest morphology.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: The specimen now referred to Rinchenia mongoliensis was first described as Oviraptor mongoliensis by Rinchen Barsbold in 1986. It was reclassified as a distinct genus, Rinchenia, by Barsbold in 1997, primarily on the basis of the uniquely tall and inflated cranial crest that differs markedly from the lower crest of Oviraptor philoceratops.

articles.title: Cranial Crest
articles.body: Rinchenia's crest is among the most prominent of any oviraptorid, forming a tall, rounded, bony dome over the skull. Such crests in oviraptorids have been compared to those of cassowaries and are generally interpreted as display structures, possibly used for species recognition, sexual selection, or intraspecific communication. The internal structure of the crest may also have resonated sound.

articles.title: Oviraptorid Biology
articles.body: Like other oviraptorids, Rinchenia had a toothless beak and robust jaws capable of crushing hard food items such as shellfish, seeds, or eggs. The omnivore designation in the PBDB reflects this dietary versatility. Oviraptorids are also known to have brooded their eggs, a behaviour confirmed by specimens preserved in brooding posture.

articles.title: Nemegt Fauna
articles.body: The Nemegt Formation preserves one of the richest and most diverse Late Cretaceous dinosaur assemblages in the world, including Tarbosaurus, Therizinosaurus, Deinocheirus, and multiple hadrosaurs and sauropods. Rinchenia was a small omnivore within this community, likely foraging opportunistically across the fluvial floodplain landscape.

record.description: Rinchenia mongoliensis was an oviraptorid from the Baruungoyot Formation of Mongolia, represented by a single partial skeleton with a crested skull, originally described as Oviraptor mongoliensis.
facts: The combination was separated from Oviraptor because of cranial and postcranial differences.
The type preserves a substantial skeleton but not a broad population sample.
Diet cannot be narrowed beyond likely omnivory or herbivory from this specimen alone.

review.ageReviewNote: The Baruungoyot Formation is late Campanian; the species should not be assigned the younger Nemegt age.
